security_audit.summary: All 14 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, Python template literals, validation messages, and expected ZIP creation. A separate medium-risk issue exists because packaging follows file symlinks and can include data outside the selected skill directory.

remediation.issue: Packaging follows file symlinks outside the skill root.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks and verify each resolved file path remains within the resolved skill directory before calling zipf.write.

semantic_findings.title: Symlink targets can escape the package root
semantic_findings.description: The packaging loop accepts file symlinks, and zipf.write follows their targets. A skill can therefore archive files outside its directory.

content.value_statement: Building reusable AI skills requires consistent structure and clear activation guidance. This skill provides a practical workflow, templates, validation, and packaging tools.
actual_capabilities: Defines a six-step workflow for planning, creating, editing, packaging, and improving AI skills.
Generates a new skill directory with SKILL.md, scripts, references, and assets folders.
Creates editable example files and marks the generated Python example as executable.
Validates required files, frontmatter fields, descriptions, resource folders, and script permissions.
Packages validated skill files into a compressed ZIP archive.
Provides concise guidance for metadata, progressive disclosure, and reusable resource selection.
limitations: The validator checks field presence with text matching and does not parse YAML semantically.
The initializer creates placeholder resources that require manual editing or removal.
The packager does not reject symlinks or verify resolved files remain inside the skill directory.
The guidance targets Claude-style skill layouts and may require adaptation for other platforms.

use_cases.title: Create a first skill
use_cases.description: Generate a standard directory, then replace placeholders with focused instructions and reusable resources.

use_cases.title: Standardize a skill library
use_cases.description: Review skill structure, frontmatter, resource placement, and packaging across a shared repository.

use_cases.title: Package domain guidance
use_cases.description: Convert specialized procedures into concise SKILL.md instructions supported by references, scripts, and assets.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a basic skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill named [name] in [directory], then identify which generated resources to keep for [workflow].
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a new skill from a clear idea.

prompt_templates.title: Refine activation guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [skill path]. Rewrite its description with specific triggers, and remove unfinished placeholders or duplicated instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Design reusable resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these usage examples: [examples]. Propose the smallest useful set of scripts, references, and assets, then update [skill path].
prompt_templates.scenario: Turning repeated work into reusable resources.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and package a skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate [skill path], resolve all reported errors and relevant warnings, then package it into [directory] and summarize the archive contents.
prompt_templates.scenario: Preparing a mature skill for distribution.

output_examples.input: Create a customer-support skill with policy references and no scripts.
output: Created a customer-support skill with focused activation guidance.
Added a references folder for policies and removed unnecessary executable resources.
Validated the structure and identified remaining content placeholders.

output_examples.input: Review and package the skill at .claude/skills/release-notes.
output: Validation passed after the missing description details were added.
Reported warnings for any remaining empty resource folders.

best_practices: Start with concrete user requests and define activation triggers before writing detailed instructions.
Keep SKILL.md concise and move extensive schemas, policies, or examples into referenced files.
Delete unused placeholders and review archive contents before distribution.
anti_patterns: Do not keep TODO text or generic descriptions in a published skill.
Do not duplicate the same guidance across SKILL.md and reference files.
Do not add scripts, references, or assets without a repeated workflow need.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete production skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. The initializer creates a structured draft with placeholders that require domain-specific editing and testing.

faq.question: What files are required?
faq.answer: Each skill needs SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter. Scripts, references, and assets are optional.

faq.question: How does validation work?
faq.answer: The validator checks structure, required frontmatter text, description quality, placeholders, resource folders, and Python script permissions.

faq.question: Where is packaged output written?
faq.answer: The packager writes a ZIP file to the chosen output directory, or the current directory when none is provided.

faq.question: Can it update existing skills?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the workflow to review instructions and resources, but the initializer refuses to overwrite an existing skill directory.

faq.question: Does packaging protect against symlink leakage?
faq.answer: No. Review and remove symlinks before packaging until resolved-path containment checks are added.
